note: The site's own words for each checked item, written to the site's rules. An item is shown only if verified_<case>.json confirmed or corrected it, it has a sentence here, and it is not in drop. group is records (the Commission's or an officer's own table or order), reported (press), or said (what a party or an official said, as reported).

cases.title: Kichha, Uttarakhand
cases.intro: Kichha is the assembly constituency in Udham Singh Nagar, a plains district on the border with Uttar Pradesh, that lost the largest share of its roll in Uttarakhand.

drop.kichha-16: The court-ordered FIR is in Haldwani, Nainital district, and does not concern Kichha.

kichha-01: The Chief Electoral Officer's table of the draft of 14 July 2026 gives Kichha a draft of 1,21,545 electors and 27,068 names left off. The same row counts 36,937 electors on the draft with an anomaly and 9,810 with no mapping to the last intensive revision, which together put them in line for a notice. It gives no reason for any name left off.
kichha-14: The Chief Electoral Officer's table of the final roll (PN 63/2026, 3 October 2026) shows 1,503 claims and 4,439 objections admitted in Kichha after the draft. That is 36.5 names removed for every 1,000 on the draft, against 14.7 in the state. Women were 2,186 of the 4,439.
kichha-02: Amar Ujala reported on 15 July 2026 that Udham Singh Nagar's draft held 11,55,672 electors and that its share of forms not collected, 13.33 per cent, was the highest of any district in the state, against 10.39 per cent for the state.
kichha-03: The Indian Express, reading the Chief Electoral Officer's presentation to parties of 3 October 2026, reported 1,77,673 names left off in Udham Singh Nagar, the second most of any district after Dehradun.
kichha-12: The Indian Express reported on 10 September 2026 that Udham Singh Nagar accounted for 43,878 of Uttarakhand's 1,30,382 Form 7 applications to delete a name, the most of any district, with 34,903 still being processed on 7 September.
kichha-06: The Times of India reported on 29 August 2026 nearly 9,300 objections in Kichha, 1,707 on the ground that the elector had shifted for good and 7,589 alleging the elector was enrolled twice. It reported that 6,412 of the second kind were filed by one booth-level agent of the BJP.
kichha-13: Hindustan Times reported on 25 September 2026 the Chief Electoral Officer's statement that about 95,000 of roughly 1.73 lakh Form 7 applications in Uttarakhand were generated by the system when electors with a notice were marked ineligible after failing or missing their hearing.
kichha-05: Kichha's Electoral Registration Officer told Newslaundry that the portal had accepted the bulk submissions, that the rules require a check when one person files many, and that no name would be deleted without a field check, a notice and a hearing.
kichha-11: The Kumaon Commissioner told The Times of India that no name would be deleted without verification, a notice and a chance for the elector to give evidence.
kichha-07: The Congress told the Election Commission in a memorandum of 20 August 2026, as The Hindu reported, that one man had filed 6,410 objections in Kichha and that 262 people in Uttarakhand had each filed more than ten Form 7s.
kichha-08: Kichha's Congress MLA alleged, as Dainik Bhaskar reported on 5 August 2026, that Form 7 objections were filed online in residents' names without their knowledge, with 90 to 95 in one name within three days. He gave the data to the Sub-Divisional Magistrate and asked for an FIR.
kichha-09: A BJP spokesperson who is a former Kichha MLA said, as The Times of India reported, that the party's own review found more than 8,000 electors on Kichha's roll also registered in Bareilly, Pilibhit and Rampur in Uttar Pradesh. No official figure for this was found.

not_found: Any statement by Kichha's Electoral Registration Officer or Udham Singh Nagar's District Election Officer on why Kichha lost the largest share of its roll, and any split of its names left off by reason.
Any count for Kichha of booth-level officers, notices issued, hearings held or electors marked ineligible after a hearing.
An official count of Form 7 applications in Kichha. The press counts differ, and the final-roll table gives only the 4,439 objections admitted.
Any FIR registered in Udham Singh Nagar over Form 7s filed in other people's names, and any court case about Kichha.
Any documented account of what in Kichha itself, such as work, housing or evictions, lies behind its figure. Only the parties' explanations were found.

cases.title: Tughlakabad, Delhi
cases.intro: Tughlakabad is the assembly constituency in Delhi's South East district that lost the largest share of its roll of the city's 70.

drop.tughlakabad-09: A single elector's story, from a profile that identifies him. The site publishes counts only.

tughlakabad-01: The Chief Electoral Officer's table of 31 August 2026 gives Tughlakabad a draft of 1,00,386 electors and 92,033 enumeration forms not collected, 47.8 of every 100 on the roll before the revision, the most of any of Delhi's 70 seats.
tughlakabad-11: The AAP won Tughlakabad in the 2025 Assembly election by 14,711 votes, so the names left off are more than six times the winning margin. That makes them large enough to decide the seat, which says nothing about whether they would have.
tughlakabad-12: The Delhi Chief Electoral Officer's office posted that special camps for all electors were held in Tughlakabad during the revision. The post gives no date and no count.
tughlakabad-04: Hindustan Times reported on 18 August 2026, from the Chief Electoral Officer's data, that when enumeration closed on 17 August only 52.14 per cent of Tughlakabad's forms had been entered, the lowest in Delhi, and that South East was the lowest district at 56.32 per cent.
tughlakabad-02: NDTV reported on 2 September 2026, citing the Election Commission's data, the same 92,033 forms not collected in Tughlakabad, followed by Okhla at 45.16 per cent.
tughlakabad-03: The Times of India reported on 1 September 2026 that South East was the district with the most forms not collected, 43.6 per cent (6,79,081 of 15,57,289).
tughlakabad-05: NDTV India reported on 18 August 2026 that Tughlakabad is home to migrant workers employed along the Faridabad border, and that experts it did not name linked the low return of forms in Tughlakabad and Okhla to this.
tughlakabad-06: In an NDTV India report from Gola Kuan and Bengali Colony on 18 August 2026, residents said workers who commute to Faridabad, Noida and Gurgaon were marked as shifted though they live there, and that tenants could not show papers such as electricity bills.
tughlakabad-10: Before enumeration began, Delhi's Chief Electoral Officer told The Indian Express on 30 June 2026 that electors whose houses had been demolished would not be found at their address, that their forms could not be collected, so they would not be on the draft, and that such cases would be dealt with separately and taken to the Election Commission. The statement was about Delhi as a whole.

not_found: Any statement by Tughlakabad's Electoral Registration Officer or South East's District Election Officer on the seat's figure, and any split of its names left off by reason from the Chief Electoral Officer.
Any count for Tughlakabad of booth-level officers, notices, hearings, or Form 6 and Form 7 applications after the draft. Delhi's final roll is due on 4 December 2026.
Any court case, party complaint or protest about Tughlakabad alone, and any statement by its MLA.
Any documented link between the seat's figure and a particular demolition or eviction.

cases.title: Danilimda, Gujarat
cases.intro: Danilimda is an Ahmedabad constituency reserved for Scheduled Castes, around Chandola Lake, where the city demolished thousands of homes in 2025. It is the one Ahmedabad seat whose final roll is smaller than its draft.

drop.dan-07: No source places the Isanpur lake demolition in Danilimda.
drop.dan-10: The petitions concern Kodinar and Sidhpur, not Danilimda.

dan-03: The Ahmedabad Municipal Corporation demolished more than 10,000 structures around Chandola Lake, in Danilimda, on 29 April and 20 May 2025, months before the revision began, as The Quint reported.
dan-01: Gujarat Samachar reported on 8 February 2026 that 634 Form 7 applications to delete names were filed in two of Danilimda's polling booths, 193 and 194, by two people it described as BJP workers, and that a complaint was registered at Isanpur police station. No outcome of the complaint was found.
dan-02: The same report described a dispute over applications to remove residents left homeless by the Chandola Lake demolitions, which alleged that their lack of papers for an address was being used to seek their deletion.
dan-06: A rights group's letter to Gujarat's Chief Electoral Officer of 17 January 2026, reported by Counterview, said residents moved from Chandola Lake were given special camps to complete their forms and that their names are on the draft. No official confirmation of the camps was found.
dan-04: Bhaskar English reported on 3 October 2026 that the municipal ward of Danilimda, which takes in the Chandola Lake area, had 19,346 fewer voters on the city's rolls in 2026 than in 2021. The paper said the fall does not show by itself how many names the revision deleted. The ward is smaller than the assembly constituency.
dan-08: BBC News Gujarati reported on 21 February 2026 that some organisations said the names and reasons of electors deleted between the draft and the final roll of 17 February had not been published, though such lists were available at the draft.
dan-09: The Hindu reported that Gujarat's election officials gave two very different counts of Form 7 applications in the state two days apart, 9,88,621 on 29 January and 1,83,235 on 31 January 2026, and that the Chief Electoral Officer did not answer its question about the gap.
dan-05: The Congress's Ahmedabad unit told Bhaskar English that many demolition drives were aimed at particular constituencies and wards, and that it had worked on voter deletions over the past year.

not_found: Any statement, release or table from Gujarat's Chief Electoral Officer or Ahmedabad's District Election Officer about Danilimda alone, including counts of Form 6 and Form 7 applications, notices and hearings.
Any reason for the 8,289 names deleted from Danilimda's roll after the draft, or for its final roll being the one in Ahmedabad smaller than its draft.
Any outcome of the police complaint over the 634 Form 7s, or any decision by the Electoral Registration Officer on them.
Any court case or documented protest about Danilimda alone.

cases.title: Murshidabad, Malda and the Dinajpurs, West Bengal
cases.intro: Murshidabad and Malda are the West Bengal districts with the most names sent to judicial officers for adjudication after the draft, close to a third of the state's. The Commission's district table, as the press printed it, sets Uttar and Dakshin Dinajpur beside them, and of the four Dakshin Dinajpur had the largest share found not eligible.

mm-07: On 2 April 2026 the Supreme Court took up on its own the surrounding of seven judicial officers at the Block Development Office in Kaliachak, Malda (Suo Motu W.P.(C) 3 of 2026). It ordered central forces wherever judicial officers were deciding revision cases, asked Malda's District Magistrate and Superintendent of Police to explain themselves, and directed that the inquiry be handed to the CBI or the NIA.
mm-02: The Election Commission's district table of adjudication outcomes, as The Indian Express printed it on 7 April 2026, gives Murshidabad 11,01,145 cases, of whom 6,33,671 were found eligible and 4,55,137 not. Malda had 8,28,127 cases, 5,88,657 and 2,39,375. Uttar Dinajpur had 4,80,341, 3,03,261 and 1,76,972. Dakshin Dinajpur had 1,32,258, 55,490 and 76,768.
mm-01: The Hindu reported that of the 60,06,675 cases under adjudication when the final roll was published on 28 February 2026, about 11 lakh were in Murshidabad and about 8 lakh in Malda, close to a third of the state's, with 4.8 lakh in Uttar Dinajpur.
mm-03: Hindustan Times reported on 8 April 2026, from the Commission's data, that Murshidabad had the most names deleted after adjudication of any district and Malda the third most, and that 58.1 per cent of Dakshin Dinajpur's cases were found not eligible.
mm-04: The Times of India reported on 10 April 2026, from the Commission's data, that Samserganj in Murshidabad lost 74,775 of its 1,08,400 names under adjudication and Lalgola 55,420 of 99,082, and that more than 37,000 of 79,683 under adjudication in Mothabari, Malda, were removed.
mm-05: The Indian Express reported on 29 March 2026 booth counts of names under adjudication that were deleted, 327 of 444 and 422 of 527 in two booths of a village in Sujapur, Malda, and 291 of 591 and 207 of 361 in booths 111 and 112 of Suti, Murshidabad.
mm-06: The New Indian Express reported that on 1 April 2026 electors deleted after adjudication surrounded seven judicial officers at the Block Development Office in Kaliachak, Malda, and blocked National Highway 12. It put Malda's adjudicated electors at about 8.30 lakh, against a district roll of 29.86 lakh.
mm-08: The Economic Times reported, from PTI, that the NIA, which took over the Mothabari case on the Supreme Court's direction, had arrested 68 people by 26 May 2026.
mm-11: SabrangIndia reported on 13 October 2026 The Wire's reading of the Commission's own figures filed with the Supreme Court. In Murshidabad, by that reading, 10.58 per cent of Form 6 applications led to a name being added, against 87.71 per cent of Form 7 requests leading to a name being deleted. In Uttar Dinajpur it was 8.16 against 96.11 per cent. The site has not read the affidavit itself.
mm-09: On a visit to Beldanga in Murshidabad, West Bengal's Chief Electoral Officer told an elector asking for deleted names to be restored that the deletions had been made by judicial officers under the Supreme Court's directions, as The New Indian Express reported on 12 April 2026. The paper put Murshidabad's deletions at 7,48,959.

not_found: Any release from the District Election Officers of Murshidabad or Malda with their own counts of adjudication, Form 6, Form 7 or hearings.
The Commission's own copy of its district table of adjudication outcomes. Only newspapers' copies were found.
Any official count, by district or constituency, of appeals decided, or of names restored after an appeal.
The reasons for adjudication outcomes by district.
Any Calcutta High Court order on adjudication in these districts.
